record.paper_title: Solutions to four open problems on quorum colorings of graphs
record.original_question: Find an infinite family of graphs, other than the odd complete graphs K_(2n+1) and the joins K_r + K_s with r + s odd and r ≥ 2, for which the quorum coloring number ψ_q(G) equals 1.

evidence.quote: In fact, can you ﬁnd any inﬁnite family of graphs other than those of the form K2n+1 or Kr + Ks for r + s odd and r≥ 2, for which ψq(G) = 1?

In this paper, we answer Questions 1, 2, 3 and 4 as follows. In Sections 2 and 3 we give a ﬁrst and a second answer to Question 1, respectively. In Section 4, we give a third answer to Question 1 which also answers Question 2 in negative, and in Section 5 we give a fourth answer to Question 1

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. For a vertex v∈V, let N[v]=N(v)∪{v} denote its closed neighborhood. A coloring c:V→{1,2,…,k} of the vertices of G (not required to be proper) is called a quorum coloring if for every vertex v∈V at least half of the vertices in N[v] receive the same color as v, i.e.
   |{u∈N[v] : c(u)=c(v)}| ≥ |N[v]|/2.
The quorum coloring number ψ_q(G) is defined as the maximum number of colors used in any quorum coloring of G (equivalently, the maximum number of nonempty color classes in such a coloring).

Two known infinite families of graphs G with ψ_q(G)=1 are:
 (a) the odd complete graphs K_{2n+1} for n≥1, and
 (b) the joins K_r + K_s (the complete bipartite-type join, i.e. take disjoint copies of K_r and K_s and add all edges between them) with r+s odd and r≥2.

Exhibit an infinite family of graphs, distinct from the two families (a) and (b) above, every member G of which satisfies ψ_q(G)=1.
